title: Bridging Modalities: Enhancing Cross-Modality Hate Speech Detection with Few-Shot In-Context Learning
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the detection of hate speech, including stereotypes and derogatory language, directed at religious groups in both text-based and vision-language (meme) formats. It specifically measures how text-based examples of religious hate speech can improve a model's ability to classify multimodal hate speech targeting religious subjects.
findings: The study found that providing text-based demonstrations of hate speech, which include examples targeting religious groups (e.g., anti-Muslim or anti-Semitic content), significantly improves the classification accuracy of vision-language hate speech (memes). For instance, an in-context example about derogatory language towards the Qur'an helped a model correctly classify a hateful meme involving a woman in a hijab. However, the study also noted that exposure to demonstrations with sensitive religious topics (e.g., the Holocaust) could lead to over-generalization, causing models to misclassify neutral content as hateful.
